questions.q: What does the optimizer actually use to produce a row-count estimate for a query plan?
options: Statistics objects, including their histograms
The index's fragmentation percentage
The number of columns in the SELECT list
The database's recovery model
questions.explain: Row-count estimation is driven by statistics — histograms and density information — not by the physical index structure itself.

questions.q: What does modification_counter, returned by sys.dm_db_stats_properties(), track?
options: The number of row modifications since the statistics object was last updated
The number of times the statistics object has ever been queried
The number of indexes on the table
The percentage of fragmentation on the associated index
questions.explain: It's the counter SQL Server's own auto-update-statistics logic watches to decide when a refresh is needed.

questions.q: What does DBCC SHOW_STATISTICS ... WITH HISTOGRAM return?
options: The histogram steps (range boundaries and row counts) that describe the actual data distribution the optimizer reads
A list of every query that has used that statistics object
The fragmentation level of the associated index
A count of duplicate indexes on the table
questions.explain: The histogram, with up to 200 steps, is the real distribution data the optimizer's cardinality estimator consults.

questions.q: Why would a DBA run UPDATE STATISTICS ... WITH FULLSCAN instead of a default UPDATE STATISTICS?
options: FULLSCAN reads every row for the most accurate histogram, useful after a large bulk load or when sampling produced a bad plan
FULLSCAN is required before any REORGANIZE operation
Default UPDATE STATISTICS does not actually change any statistics at all
FULLSCAN is always faster than a sampled update
questions.explain: Sampling is fast but can miss the true distribution on a large or skewed table; FULLSCAN trades scan cost for maximum accuracy.

questions.q: With AUTO_UPDATE_STATISTICS_ASYNC enabled, what happens when a query triggers an automatic statistics update?
options: The triggering query uses the existing (old) statistics while the update happens in the background
The triggering query is cancelled until the update finishes
Statistics updates are disabled entirely
The update always uses WITH FULLSCAN regardless of table size
questions.explain: Async mode avoids making the triggering query wait synchronously for the refreshed statistics.
